transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-08 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Jordan (Helix Head of MLOps), Priya (Helix Platform Eng), Sam (Helix CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're Maya and Ravi from Redwood, and lena joins for the infra questions. Jordan, want to kick off with your goals?
[00:14] Jordan: Yeah sure, thanks. We're reworking inference infra for Helix's recommendation engine — need predictable latencies and cost control. Basically evaluating hosted vs dedicated, and whether we need private VPCs. Timeframe is Q3 pilot.
[00:28] Priya: to add, our main concerns are isolation for PII-ish features, burst spikes around batch promotions, and cold start warmup for large models.
[00:40] Ravi: Got it. Can you describe your burst profile? like QPS baseline vs peaks and duration? even ballparks help us size reserved pools.
[00:52] Jordan: Baseline is 250 qps, peaks up to 2.2k for 5-20 minutes during campaigns, with a longer daily swell ~45 minutes at ~800 qps. We also do async batches overnight.
[01:10] Lena: okay, and what's your SLAs today? P95 latency targets?
[01:16] Sam: P95 target is 200ms for short responses, under 600ms for longer generations. For some internal use cases we tolerate higher.
[01:27] Maya: That helps. For dedicated we'll talk about reserved GPU pools sized for steady-state plus a burst strategy that can 'borrow' hosted capacity. We typically recommend sized pool for baseline and a burst buffer for campaigns.
[01:40] Priya: Curious about isolation—do dedicated GPUs give us full tenant isolation? or is there still hypervisor multi-tenancy?
[01:49] Ravi: With Redwood Dedicated, we can do node-level isolation: you get pinned GPUs and dedicated compute nodes inside a tenant-dedicated VPC. There's also options for VM-level or even physical isolation for on-prem deployments. There's still network overlay but compute isn't shared.
[02:05] Jordan: any noisy neighbor concerns on the same rack? we've had bad experiences with PCIe throttling when other tenants force big sync ops.
[02:14] Ravi: We schedule jobs to avoid colocating heavy training jobs, and we prefer GPUs with MIG or H100 partitioning for finer isolation. However while hardware-level contention is rare, it can happen; for strictest cases we recommend private on-prem or single-tenant metal.
[02:32] Priya: What about prewarming? our cold starts of a 70B model take minutes which kills UX.
[02:38] Lena: We support pinned warm instances and long-lived workers holding KV cache warm. There's a memory cost tradeoff. You can keep a pool of warm workers at cost. Also prefix/KV caching helps because many requests reuse similar prefixes.
[02:52] Jordan: hmm, KV cache — is that per-process or shared?
[02:57] Ravi: It's per-serving-process, generally; we do automatic prefix caching at the routing layer which can serve from cache if the prefix matches. Cache hit rates from your traces will drive how effective it is.
[03:10] Jordan: Got  — our prefix hit is about 18% during peaks. Is that enough to materially reduce tokens?
[03:17] Lena: 18% helps but it's not massive. We usually see cost reductions when hit rates are >30% for chatty workloads. But batching and request consolidation also cut token cost.
[03:30] Sam: If we do a hybrid (reserved + hosted burst), what's the failure mode? if hosted capacity is overloaded during a big incident, do we have graceful degradation?
[03:40] Maya: Yes — typical patterns: tiered fallback to a lower-cost smaller model, queueing with rate-limit windows, and finally returning cached responses or degraded responses. We can configure automatic model fallbacks and route traffic to hosted variants in other regions.
[03:55] Priya: how about data residency—if we route to hosted during bursts, does that send PII outside our VPC? that's a hard no for some features.
[04:03] Ravi: Good catch. For regulated features we recommend Dedicated with private control plane or Private deployment. Hosted burst would move data outside unless you use our VPC peering/Private path feature. There's also encryption-at-rest and KMS options.
[04:18] Jordan: We're likely to mix: Dedicated for PII workloads, hosted-burst for non-sensitive recommendations. Price-wise, what's the delta if we keep a 10-GPU reserved pool vs purely hosted?
[04:29] Maya: We'll send a detailed rubric, but very roughly reserved gives unit-cost savings when you consistently use >50% of the pool. There's a fixed monthly charge for reserved GPUs. Hosted is elastic but higher per-token. We can model your traces.
[04:44] Sam: For the benchmark, can you simulate our 2.2k spikes for 20 minutes to see queuing and tail latencies?
[04:51] Ravi: Yes — action item for us to run a 48-hour with scripted spikes. We'll test H100 profiles and A100 to show tradeoffs. Also measure cold starts, warm worker hit rates, and queue times.
[05:05] Priya: A technical nit—what's your approach to multi-GPU model sharding vs tensor parallelism? for our 70B we plan ZeRO or model parallel; does Redwood handle that?
[05:16] Lena: The serving runtime supports model parallel shards and tensor parallel kernels depending on model backend. We pick kernels and quant strategies automatically, but for complicated custom sharding we can work with you on model packaging.
[05:29] Jordan: Any limits on long context lengths? we sometimes extend to 32k tokens in experiments.
[05:34] Ravi: We support longer sequences but performance and memory tradeoffs increase. For 32k you often need H100 or sharded configs, and latency will increase. We'll capture that in the benchmark.
[05:46] Maya: Quick question for procurement: do you have compliance requirements—SOC2, ISO, SSO?
[05:51] Jordan: SOC2 is required, SAML SSO and role-based access. Also audit logs for model versioning and request tracing.
[05:59] Maya: We'll share SOC2 docs, SSO integration guide, and our audit log capabilities. We support KMS and customer-managed keys in Private.
[06:10] Priya: Our ops team wants observability: per-route p95/p99 breakdowns and token cost per request. Is that in console?
[06:16] Lena: Yes, console exposes token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-model traces. You can also hook into tracing for your internal monitoring.
[06:25] Jordan: Let's surface failure scenarios: what happens if a dedicated node goes down mid-peak?
[06:30] Ravi: We do automatic failover—requests are routed to remaining capacity and hosted fallback if enabled. There's brief degradation while caches refill; warm caches aren't replicated cross-nodes by default.
[06:42] Sam: That refill time is concerning. Are there patterns to replicate KV cache?
[06:46] Lena: You can use periodic checkpointing of important prefixes or run a small set of standby warm workers holding critical caches. It's a tradeoff: cost vs warm recovery time.
[06:57] Priya: Network egress — do you support private peering for on-prem? we don't want traffic transiting public internet for PII.
[07:05] Ravi: Yes, we offer VPC peering and private link variants. For on-prem we can run a private package behind your firewall; data never leaves your network if you choose the on-prem option.
[07:16] Jordan: About SLAs — what uptime and latency SLAs exist for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:23] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA on uptime and latency targets based on committed capacity tiers. Hosted has best-effort SLAs but we publish performance profiles. We'll include the SLA table in the follow-up.
[07:34] Priya: One more — how are updates/rollouts handled? can we pin to a model version during pilot?
[07:40] Lena: You can pin versions, do canary rollouts, and set automatic fallback to previous version if regressions hit. Rollouts are per-route.
[07:50] Jordan: for the initial pilot we'd like 8 GPUs reserved (for baseline), with ability to burst to 40 GPUs hosted. is that model reasonable?
[07:59] Ravi: That's a common pattern. We'll validate with your traces; often customers reserve enough for steady-state and use hosted for short peaks. We'll also quantify queueing during the ramp.
[08:10] Sam: Could burst credits be pre-purchased so we don't get surprise costs during big campaigns?
[08:15] Maya: Yes we offer burst credit packages and committed burst pools. We'll include pricing options.
[08:21] Priya: curious about metrics we'll get during benchmark — can we get per-token cost breakdown and skew by endpoint?
[08:27] Lena: Absolutely. We'll provide token cost, average latency, p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and cache hit rates per endpoint.
[08:36] Jordan: Any red flags from your side about our plan?
[08:39] Ravi: The only gaps are cache hit rate (18% is low) and cold-start strategy. If you can increase prefix reuse or accept warm worker cost, the economics change a lot. Also consider whether PII paths can be fully isolated; otherwise fallback routing is a blocker.
[08:58] Maya: Great — to recap next steps: Helix to share traffic traces and prompt set; Redwood to run benchmark and send pricing + SOC2 + SLA table. We'll tentatively schedule a network review.
[09:14] Jordan: sounds good. One last quick detail — inter-region latency matters for some customers in EU. If we do multi-region fallback, will that affect SLA?
[09:22] Lena: We'll measure the cross-region tail and include options: regional fallback vs degrade to smaller model within-region. Both affect latency and cost.
[09:34] Sam: ok thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the traces by Monday.
[09:39] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and artifact links.
